code_level_evidence.CoverPickerModal.tsx: renders Arco <Modal visible={visible} onCancel={onCancel} .../> as a JSX sibling of <Drawer>, not a JSX child (src/components/admin/geography/GeographyListViewClient.tsx lines ~367-490)
code_level_evidence.arco Modal source (node_modules/@arco-de: onEscExit calls event.stopPropagation() before onCancel() when escToExit && visible && event.key === Esc.key; escToExit defaults to true and is not overridden by CoverPickerModal
code_level_evidence.arco Drawer source (node_modules/@arco-d: Drawer has its OWN independent onKeyDown handler bound directly to its own portal wrapper div (also escToExit-gated), not to document and not to any ancestor shared with Modal's wrapper
code_level_evidence.conclusion: Modal and Drawer are separate DOM portal subtrees (both default to document.body as popup container) each with an independently-scoped onKeyDown handler. A keydown originating inside the Modal's subtree can only bubble through the Modal's own DOM ancestors, not into the Drawer's separate subtree -- architecturally Escape cannot double-close both. Combined with the stopPropagation() call, this gives strong (but not live-keypress-tested) confidence the Step-8 requirement holds.
